gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-merriweather: Wobbly, playful blobs up top, with bowls nearly sealed. Merriweather Sans follows in a plain sans with tall, sturdy lowercase and an open-eyed e, so a long page moves along without any of the heading's slowness.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-epilogue: Woodgod has a vintage, commanding look, with wide channels into every bowl and lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals. And Epilogue runs on a wire-like monoline stroke with stubby ascenders, so paragraphs flow smoothly without any brush-like swelling.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-archivo: Outrun Future draws a synthwave outline of constant width that you could trace with a finger, spaced wide apart. But Archivo keeps long text approachable, its curves opening outward under a large x-height, so paragraphs feel sturdy and unhurried.
gen-dafont-redux-fs-merriweather-sans: Contemporary and geometric, Redux spreads its wide-spaced letters and enlarged lowercase across the line, with thinner hairlines. Merriweather Sans takes over beneath with sturdy tall lowercase and an e that opens to the right, giving the heading a clean, grounded companion.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-archivo: Bold, heavy letters with a stencil-cut flatness lead here. Archivo gives it a counterweight: its curves open outward, and that open sans against the closed heading shapes is the pair's real charm.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-glegoo: Glegoo reads refined and spacious, with big counters in a tall lowercase and curves that stay wide open. New Title's chain-linked boldness against it is the whole appeal.
gen-audiowide-montserrat: Montserrat reads like a line of wire gliding past the eye, with generous openings leading into each curve. Audiowide does futuristic, tile-like punch best, while Montserrat does the quiet, approachable work of carrying the words.
gen-dafont-stencilia-satoshi: Structural and striking, with spacious curve gaps up top. Satoshi's soaring x-height and single stroke width set against the heading's shifting weight is where this pairing gets its distinct personality.
gen-dafont-stentiga-work-sans: Luxurious and refined, Stentiga spreads its letters out with wide openings and sturdy crossbars. Then Work Sans steps in with a high mean line and open c tips, so the modern text sits comfortably under that spacious heading.
gen-gf-autour-one-switzer: Switzer reads like tubular wire, with a tall waist line and c tips that never close in toward each other. Autour One makes it bold and expressive above.
